content:
According to 404 Media, Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass an iPhone security feature that automatically restarts the device if it has not been unlocked for 72 consecutive hours. Details below.

Background

Nearly two years ago, Apple introduced the "Inactivity Reboot" feature in the iOS 18.1 update, which forces an iPhone to restart after 72 consecutive hours without being unlocked.

Essentially, this feature makes it harder for law enforcement agencies and forensic tools to access data on a locked iPhone, because restarting the device causes it to return to a "Before First Unlock" (BFU) state, rather than remaining in the less restrictive "After First Unlock" (AFU) state.

When an iPhone is in BFU state, some sensitive data remains protected by encryption keys; these keys only become available after the user enters their passcode for the first time, at which point the device enters AFU state.

From that moment, more data on the device can be accessed, until the iPhone restarts again and returns to BFU state.

The iPhone will automatically restart, meaning that even if the device is seized by law enforcement, it may return to BFU state before investigators can access it, since obtaining a search warrant or transporting the device to a forensic laboratory both take time.

As 404 Media noted when iOS 18.1 was released, this feature also makes it harder for thieves or other criminals to keep a stolen device in AFU state long enough to develop or use cracking methods.

GrayKey Reportedly Can Bypass "Inactivity Reboot" Feature

404 Media reported today that, according to a "training video produced for law enforcement and apparently dated early 2025," Magnet Forensics, which develops the GrayKey phone unlocking tool, appears to have developed a method to bypass the iPhone's "Inactivity Reboot" feature.

The report states that Magnet has developed a new device called GrayKey Preserve, and has added an "Evidence Preservation Mode" to its existing GrayKey hardware.

Both are reportedly designed to maintain the iPhone's forensic state while not immediately exposing the data stored on the device, allowing law enforcement agencies to maintain that state while waiting for search authorisation.

The report points out that, although the video does not detail the technical principles of the bypass mechanism, it explains that GrayKey can keep the iPhone in AFU state even when it restarts.

404 Media separately reached out to Apple and Magnet Forensics for comment, but neither responded to requests for comment. They also consulted iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen, who said Magnet may have found a way to manipulate the iPhone's clock, or to completely shut down the mechanism responsible for causing some data to expire and become invalid.

Although the video appears to be from early 2025, it remains unclear how long this technology has been available to law enforcement agencies, whether it has been used in actual investigations, and whether the bypass method is still effective against the latest version of iOS.
